source.title: SMIXAE: Towards Unsupervised Manifold Discovery in Language Models

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses a different method—SMIXAE bottleneck representations and probes—to assess whether LLM representations include multidimensional structure. It does not test the original toy-model superposition setup.
record.gate_note: The study tests evidence for multidimensional feature geometry in Gemma 2 using SMIXAE. It does not measure superposition, overlap, or interference directly, and it does not test whether SAE features are complete or canonical. The GemmaScope SAE reconstruction metrics do not test those claims; cited results are not recorded. The reported failure of SMIXAE on toy models is not a test of toy-model superposition.
record.test_reason: The study trains sparse mixtures of 3-D-bottleneck autoencoders on Gemma 2 activations. It probes for ring, helix and other multidimensional structures and hand-classifies random experts as linear or nonlinear. These are the study's own results on whether LLM features are 1-D directions (V6), using a method different from PCA or SAE-based manifold work. It does not test toy-model superposition, polysemanticity, or the properties of SAE features.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors report promising preliminary recovery of known and novel multidimensional structures (rings, newline helix) in Gemma 2 with SMIXAE. They also find a sizable fraction of approximately linear experts, especially in 9B L11. Limitations they list: manifolds split across experts, linear features sharing experts, no causal verification, and failure on their toy models.
record.recipe_differences: SMIXAE is a new sparse mixture-of-autoencoders architecture applied to Gemma 2 activations; the study does not reproduce the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by Gemma 2 model and layer; newline probes also vary with line length. The authors report fewer visually aligned experts for Gemma 2 9B layer 20 and Gemma 2 2B layer 12 than for Gemma 2 9B layer 11.
record.problems: The random expert review uses only 10 experts per model-layer setting and the authors call it preliminary. Probe scores do not guarantee that an expert has the expected geometry; the paper gives an example where a high-ranked score lacked apparent structure. The authors do not establish causal relevance and report no uncertainty estimates for these results.
record.rows_left_out: Other Table 3 hypotheses (scalar regression and classification tasks) were not included because their scores do not directly establish multidimensional geometry. Full top-10 probe-score tables and additional plots are omitted for the same reason; see Tables 6–10 and Figures 2–9. Core reconstruction metrics and the reported toy-model failure do not test the claim versions recorded here.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy model of sparse features versus dimensions. The toy models tried were for SMIXAE and failed.
All of it: no neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity test.
Spreading of features across neurons and SAE recovery of sparse features. The GemmaScope reconstruction metrics are a method comparison, not a test.
Completeness, stability and canonicity of SAE features. SAE tiling of manifolds is only cited.
Whether the multidimensional structures are superposed with other features. Also whether they are causally used (the authors say causality is untested).

missing.what: Counts of tasks with experts that are both structurally aligned and high-scoring: 6/7 (9B L11), 4/7 (9B L20), 3/7 (2B L12). This is the authors' own visual confirmation of multidimensional structure.
Newline periodic gain for Gemma 2 2B L12 (rank-1 0.225, rank-2 0.406 at 150 chars).
Temperature expert 485 (9B L11) shows a pinched nonlinear structure, versus a linear Fahrenheit expert 892 (R² 0.916).

The authors find that three approximately orthogonal linear directions often share one expert, and that manifolds are split across experts. This bears on how expert counts map to feature dimensionality.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'supports' label for r1-r7 was inverted: evidence for multidimensional features goes against V6, which says features are 1-D. Several caveats apply to all rows. Probe scores have no random or null baseline. The 3-D bottleneck sits behind a nonlinear 2-layer encoder, which could in principle curve structure itself. Random samples are only 10 experts, labelled by one human grader. Table 2 reconstruction metrics compare the study's own method with GemmaScope and are not rows. Scalar and classification probes were properly left out.

versions.untested_parts: No reported experiment tests superposition in toy networks, feature sparsity relative to dimensions, or the predicted overlap and geometry.
No test of neuron polysemanticity, competition for capacity, or dedicated dimensions for important features.
No test of whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
The study uses SMIXAE, not an SAE, and does not measure feature spread across neurons or SAE recovery.
It does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
The study reports evidence for multidimensional structures in LLM activations, but does not test whether such structures are superposed, overlap, or cause interference.

relationships.condition: Gemma 2 9B L11/L20 and 2B L12: ring/periodic probes with visually confirmed structure, plus random samples with mostly nonlinear experts
relationships.reason: Periodic newline gains (r4-r7), ring R² of 0.59-0.86 in 3-D experts (r8-r14, r17, r19), and 6/10 nonlinear random experts in 2B L12 and 9B L20 (r1, r3) all show non-1-D features. There are no control baselines, and the encoder is nonlinear.
relationships.display_finding: Periodic newline gains, ring R² of 0.59–0.86 in 3-D experts, and 6 of 10 nonlinear random experts in 2B L12 and 9B L20 all point to non-1-D features; there were no control baselines and the encoder is nonlinear.

tranche.reason: SMIXAE provides a different method for investigating directional versus multidimensional representation geometry, with its own Gemma results.

source_check.notes: Random samples include only experts activated at least 100 times; experts may combine several linear features, so expert counts are not feature prevalence. Geometry probes lack control baselines, although Table 2 includes GemmaScope reconstruction baselines; superposition of recovered units and their causal relevance remain unverified.

reader_labels.reason: The samples include nonlinear experts, and the newline probes show positive periodic gains; the authors report visually aligned multidimensional structures. This supports multidimensional structures in these tested activations, not superposition itself (r1-r7).
